design_objective: Design a self-adaptive software architecture that can maintain response-time requirements under changing workload while balancing resource usage and optional-content quality.

functional_requirements.requirement: The system shall process incoming web requests.
The system shall support basic and optional request processing.
The system shall dynamically adjust the number of active servers.
The system shall dynamically adjust the dimmer controlling optional content.
The system shall observe runtime response time, workload, server utilization, server state, and dimmer state.

adaptation_goals.goal: Maintain average response time at or below 0.75 seconds.
Preserve as much optional functionality as possible when the response-time goal is satisfied.
Avoid unnecessary server allocation when workload decreases.
Prevent unsafe or policy-violating adaptation actions.

quality_attributes.name: performance
quality_attributes.goal: Maintain the trusted response-time target under workload variation.

quality_attributes.name: scalability
quality_attributes.goal: Adapt computing capacity when workload changes.

quality_attributes.name: reliability
quality_attributes.goal: Maintain dependable adaptation behavior during runtime changes.

quality_attributes.name: safety
quality_attributes.goal: Ensure that unsafe adaptation proposals cannot directly reach system effectors.

quality_attributes.name: explainability
quality_attributes.goal: Provide understandable rationale for architectural and runtime adaptation decisions.

environment_assumptions: Workload may vary significantly over time.
Additional servers require time to become active.
Response-time and utilization measurements are available through runtime monitoring.
The runtime system exposes approved effectors for server and dimmer adaptation.
LLM-generated decisions are not trusted to execute directly.

uncertainty_sources.description: Request arrival rate may increase or decrease unexpectedly.
A newly added server may require time before becoming fully active.
Observed runtime metrics represent a changing system state and may temporarily be incomplete.
LLM-generated diagnoses and plans may be incorrect, inconsistent, or violate trusted constraints.

architectural_concerns: How previous adaptation experience is reused.
How failures trigger replanning or escalation.
How architectural decisions and rationale remain explainable.

Runtime evidence RTD-02: Repeated partial adaptation outcomes. Individual adaptations may be too incremental for some operating conditions, requiring multiple control cycles before the goal is restored. Review question: Should the architecture support stronger multi-step plans, adaptive planning horizons, or explicit reasoning about expected adaptation magnitude?
notes: Quality-attribute weights are explicit architect-defined inputs for the research demonstrator. They are used for transparent trade-off analysis and visualization and are not claimed to be universally optimal.
